host.isolation: Both launchers fix the Compose project at synveda-evaluation and check that volume name engine-wide. This host's engine already holds synveda-evaluation volumes from 2026-09-20, so the drill used its own engine, which started with no images, containers or volumes. The host's synveda-evaluation volumes kept their 2026-09-20 creation times.
host.architecture_note: first published pair drilled on linux/arm64; the v0.4.6 -> v0.4.7 drill ran on a linux/amd64 Docker Desktop VM

environment_note: The first v0.4.7 preparation was refused with 'generate-secrets: secret parent directory metadata was refused' before any container or volume existed: Alpine's adduser had given the drill HOME the setgid bit, so the state directories were mode 2700 and the launcher requires exactly 700. The partial state (an empty lock and installation.json) was removed, the bit cleared, and the next preparation passed. This is a drill-setup artifact.

digest_method: snapshot.py: one REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction as the bundled superuser synveda_owner over the local socket, so row-level security hides nothing; per public table, row count and SHA-256 over the sorted row_to_json text of its columns, with the column set frozen from the snapshot before the upgrade, so columns a migration adds do not change the digest of existing data; ledger digest over version:checksum; audit prefix digest over seq, prev_hash, hash, occurred_at, actor, action, resource, outcome, payload and trace_id up to a bound. This differs from the v0.4.6 -> v0.4.7 drill, which read tenant tables as synveda_gateway under forced RLS.
